item.title: Northern Health adjusts Tumbler Ridge shuttle to once-daily
item.description: Beginning on February 24th, the shuttle will depart from Tumbler Ridge at 7 a.m. and will return to Tumbler Ridge at 7:45 p.m.

item.title: B.C. police release photo of now-deported extortion suspect in appeal for information
item.description: SURREY — Police in Surrey, B.C., have released the image of a foreign national suspected of involvement in a wave of extortion gripping the region. item.title: B.C. approves expansion of open-pit Copper Mountain mine in southern Interior
item.description: VICTORIA — The British Columbia government has approved the expansion of an open-pit copper and gold mine in the province’s southern Interior. A statement from Ministry of Mining and Critical Minerals says B.C. has issued permits under mines and environmental management legislation for the New Ingerbelle expansion at the Copper Mountain mine near Princeton. item.title: RCMP arrests relative of Tumbler Ridge shooter
item.description: The RCMP have arrested a man who is related to the Tumbler Ridge shooter on multiple charges including a Canada-wide warrant for attempted murder.

item.title: Crystal Cup finishes amid frigid temperatures on Charlie Lake
item.description: The Crystal Cup Pond Hockey Challenge had 56 teams competing across all divisions this weekend on the surface of Charlie Lake.

item.title: Canadian Red Cross raises more than $1 million to Tumbler Ridge
item.description: The Canadian Red Cross has raised more than $1 million for the community impacted by the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School shooting.

item.title: Eby says it looks like OpenAI could have prevented ‘horrific’ Tumbler Ridge killings
item.description: British Columbia Premier David Eby says it "looks like" OpenAI had the opportunity to prevent the recent mass shootings in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.
